purpose: The 6–8 varied client-report briefs #360 asks for, chosen before any implementation comparison and held fixed through the #362 checkpoint: the same ids run against the current product and against the report milestone, three times each, so the delta is between products and not between questions.

briefs.why: Low density, two options to weigh and one to recommend: the argument carries the document, and a report that leans on figures it does not have shows it.
Low density with one three-way count (34 / 29 / 19 datapoints) that belongs in a table, and a conclusion about what the first report cannot say.
High density: workstreams against plan (118%, 41%, 33%), banked against target, named decisions and owners — a data table with a note is the natural centre.
High density with a segmented book (12% below cost, 40% near it, top 15% at 34% margin) and three repricing tiers, each with expected churn: tiers as table rows and as chart categories.
Four country names as categories, two payback cases over 26 and 34 months as series, and three named entry conditions: the widest chart labels in the corpus.
A headcount bridge year by year — a chart whose categories are years and whose series are hires, attrition and mix — beside a costed plan that has to be argued in prose.
Medium density whose hardest requirement is text: who loses access if counters close has to be said plainly, at length, next to a channel table.
A sequence with six-month milestones and a stated cost of deferral: the recommendation is a timeline in prose, with the synergy figures in support.
